conflicts.description: The Curtain Call Company must steal the earring from the Court of Gilded Masks before it awakens, while the Silent Overture schemes to ensure it does.
conflicts.name: The Heist of the Obsidian Earring

conflicts.description: The Lanternwrights' Guild hunts the thieves for meddling with relics, even as their own vaults grow too fragile to hold them.
conflicts.name: Wardens Against Illusionists

description: Velmire is a gaslamp fantasy city smothered in perpetual fog, where brass streetlamps burn with captured aether and aristocrats float their entertainments above the rooftops. Beneath the glitter, cursed antiquities surface from the drowned old quarters and change hands in whispers. A troupe of stage magicians, celebrated by day, moonlights as thieves who relieve the powerful of their dangerous heirlooms. Their latest commission is the most perilous yet: to steal the Obsidian Earring from a duchess's floating ball before the artifact awakens and devours the shadow of every guest. The tone is mischievous and sly, full of misdirection, velvet curtains and wry bargains, written for an adult audience that enjoys wit alongside menace. Every shadow in Velmire is treated as a person's quiet double, and losing one is a slow, terrible unmaking.

factions.description: The crew of stage magicians who steal cursed antiquities by night. They rely on illusion, sleight of hand and carefully staged distractions, and they keep a code against harming the innocent.
factions.name: The Curtain Call Company

factions.description: The duchess's masked aristocratic circle, who treat intrigue as a performance and collect rare curses as trophies. Their pageantry hides a fear of losing status, and their shadows.
factions.name: The Court of Gilded Masks

factions.description: Artisans and wardens who maintain the city's aether lamps and secretly guard its most perilous relics. They answer to ancient oaths and distrust both thieves and nobles.
factions.name: The Lanternwrights' Guild

factions.description: A hushed cult of collectors who believe the Obsidian Earring should awaken, and who work behind the scenes to ensure it does.
factions.name: The Order of the Silent Overture

history.description: A strange fog rolled in from the sea and never lifted, hiding the city's old quarter and ending the era of open skies.
history.name: The Great Fog Descent

history.description: A tidal surge drowned the old shopping gallery, burying its relics and giving rise to the black market of cursed antiquities.
history.name: The Flooding of the Arcade

history.description: The Lanternwrights' Guild locked the most dangerous relics behind felt and silence after a theatre troupe lost its shadows to a cursed mask.
history.name: The Sealing of the Velvet Vault

history.description: Duchess Ilvane's house tethered its ballroom to the clouds and acquired the Obsidian Earring at auction, inviting the whole court to admire it.
history.name: The Raising of the Aerie

locations.description: A crumbling opera house in the Fogwharf district. Its trapdoors, counterweights and mirror-lined wings serve as the thieves' workshop and hideout, and its stage lights cast the sharpest shadows in the city.
locations.name: The Gilded Lantern Theatre

locations.description: A ballroom suspended beneath moored aether balloons high above Velmire. Chandeliers of captured lightning light the dance floor, and the Obsidian Earring is displayed in a glass reliquary at its heart.
locations.name: The Aerie of Duchess Ilvane

locations.description: A flooded Victorian-style shopping gallery in the old quarter where cursed antiquities surface at low tide. Black-market auctions are held on its drowned mezzanines by lantern light.
locations.name: The Sunken Arcade

locations.description: A hidden strongroom lined with plush curtains and silencing felt, kept by the Lanternwrights' Guild. Dangerous relics are locked here, and its walls are said to hold back any shadow that wanders too far.
locations.name: The Velvet Vault

name: Velmire, City of Borrowed Fog

rules.statement: Every living person's shadow is a quiet double of their vitality; a person whose shadow is devoured grows pale, forgetful and eventually fades from the world.
Cursed antiquities awaken when exposed to a crowd of living shadows under bright artificial light, and sleep again only in felt-lined darkness.
Aether lamps provide light and mechanical power, but they cannot burn near an awakened relic without flickering out.
Weapons and machines in Velmire run on clockwork, steam and compressed aether; explosive powders are unknown and no firearms exist.
The perpetual fog muffles sound and scatters light, so distances are hard to judge and secrets travel by whisper and signal lantern.
Only noble houses licensed by the Crown may moor floating estates above the city, making height a visible mark of rank.
Etiquette in Velmire demands theatrical flourish; an insult delivered without wit is considered more scandalous than the insult itself.
